chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Uqba ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who said, 'This ship is for so-and-so,' and did not specify what was in it, and there was food in it. Should the man be given the ship and what is in it? He (peace be upon him) said: 'It belongs to the one to whom it was bequeathed, unless the owner is accused (of insolvency or deceit), and there is nothing for the inheritors.'

key_terms.لِفُلَانٍ: For so-and-so (generic name used in examples)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on inheriting the contents of a bequeathed ship or container when not explicitly specified?
ai.summary: In this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the principle of 'general inclusion' (al-mutlaq bi-al-maqyud) is applied to maritime bequests, establishing that unspecified contents are presumed part of the gift unless the testator is 'mutahham' (suspected of hidden debts). This highlights the Shia juristic distinction between a simple bequest and the preservation of heirs' rights, ensuring that the beneficiary receives the vessel and its cargo unless financial encumbrances necessitate liquidation for debt settlement.
